title: Dynamic Routes Basics
description: Create pages that adapt to any parameter like /posts/123 using [id].js and the useRouter hook.

slides.title: When Static Isn't Enough 🔀
slides.content:
# The Problem

You have a blog with hundreds of posts. Creating a separate file for each is impossible.

**Solution: Dynamic Routes.**

A single file can handle an infinite number of paths using **bracket notation**:

* `pages/posts/[id].js` → matches `/posts/1`, `/posts/hello-world`, etc.

Next.js extracts the dynamic part and passes it to your component.

slides.title: First Dynamic Page (pages/posts/[id].js)
slides.content: Any file with `[param]` in its name becomes a dynamic route. Use the router to read the value.

quizData.question: Which file would you create to handle the route `/product/xyz`?
quizData.explanation: The bracket syntax creates a dynamic segment. `[slug].js` will match any value like `xyz`.

slides.title: Reading the Parameter 📖
Pre‑rendered Dynamic Page (pages/posts/[id].js)
slides.content: Combine dynamic routes with data fetching. `getStaticProps` receives `params`.

quizData.question: In `pages/posts/[id].js`, where do you find the `id` value during server‑side rendering (in `getStaticProps`)?
quizData.explanation: Data fetching functions like `getStaticProps` receive `params` directly from the context, not the client‑side router.
